# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 5
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 5

---

*[Thomas departs from Gundaphorus. He encounters a talking colt/foal of a donkey. The wild ass.]*

1. And when Thomas had baptized Gundaphorus and his brother Gad, he went out from them and traveled to another city.

2. And as he went along the road there met him a wild ass's colt, and it spoke to Thomas and said: "Twin of Christ and fellow apostle, why do you travel on foot and weary yourself? Sit on me and ride."

3. And Thomas marveled at this and said: "Who has endowed you with speech, O animal?"

4. And the colt said: "I am of the race of that ass on which your Lord sat when he entered Jerusalem; and I was kept for this, that you also should sit on me. For it is right that those who preach should ride on asses."

5. And Thomas smiled and said: "You say well."

6. And he sat on the colt and rode, and the colt went a long way.

7. And the multitude of the people who were coming and going on the road marveled, for they saw a wild ass carrying a man.

8. And as they went, they came to an inn, and the colt carried Thomas into it.

9. And when they had entered, Thomas dismounted from the colt.

10. And the colt said to Thomas: "You have received the completion of your sign, O apostle of Christ the Most High."

11. "But now I beg you — give me freedom to go to my own place, for I am not able to eat with people, nor to drink what they drink."

12. And Thomas said to the colt: "The one who gave you this speech will lead you back to your place."

13. And the colt bowed down before Thomas and went away.

14. And Thomas watched him go and gave thanks to God for the wonders that had appeared.

---
*EMET note: The talking colt claims descent from the Palm Sunday ass (Matt 21:7). This establishes apostolic typology — as the Lord rode into Jerusalem on an ass, Thomas rides to India. The phrase "twin of Christ" (*taw'ma d'Mshiha*) is the Syriac etymological play on Thomas = twin.*
